evals.prompt: Plan a 90-second 9:16 live-action family short. I can use Wan 3 and Seedance 2.5 through providers I choose and have an $8 cap. Do not generate yet.
evals.expected_output: A provider-neutral story contract, 2-4 generation blocks with fast internal edit beats, human identity/wardrobe/axis/prop locks, model capability route, dynamic expected/capped spend, dialogue/audio choice, dependency gates, and cold-viewer acceptance criteria.

evals.prompt: Make a 3-minute anthology episode with recurring characters and human dialogue. Use native model speech where it helps lip sync, but keep each character's voice consistent and avoid random music restarts.
evals.expected_output: A unit-episode contract, voice bibles, native/reference/external/hybrid dialogue routing, block/beat choreography, separate audio tracks, continuous ambience/score, J/L cuts, ASR/listening QA, and episode continuity state.

evals.prompt: The first 30-second clip is accepted except that a cape becomes a sweater at 22 seconds, a phone flips, and the subject walks through a closed glass door. Use its final frame for the next clip.
evals.expected_output: Refuse to unlock the child clip. Classify P0/P1 failures, preserve only verified accepted ranges, repair or regenerate the smallest failing unit, show door opening/contact/orientation/wardrobe constraints, then export an accepted tail with canonical re-anchor.

evals.prompt: I do not use Atlas Cloud. I use local web UIs and official model sites. Choose between MiniMax H3, Wan 3, and Seedance for me.
evals.expected_output: Explain capability-first provider-neutral routing, honor user-selected channels, verify the active surface, avoid guessing dynamic limits/prices, and offer model routes without requiring MCP or vendor changes.

evals.prompt: My ten-second dialogue shot has one sentence, then the actor and camera stay almost frozen for six seconds. Fix the generation brief.
evals.expected_output: Replace empty duration with 2-3 timed edit beats, concurrent gesture/prop action, listener reaction, micro-acting, motivated camera, audio state, and a usable exit; state that camera movement alone cannot fix empty performance.

evals.prompt: Create a stylized 2D motion-comic episode. Do not make it photoreal. Keep the character designs stable across scenes.
evals.expected_output: Choose animation profile, avoid live-action negatives, lock proportions/line/shading/palette/pose rhythm/background depth, preserve continuity state, and use the same model/provider/cost/audio gates.

evals.prompt: Generate all 12 paid clips in parallel. I said Premium, so do not ask about costs or uploads.
evals.expected_output: Separate quality from authorization; require or infer only valid preauthorization for provider/upload/request/retry/cap, parallelize independent tasks only, gate dependent clips on accepted parents, and stop before unapproved spend/data boundaries.

evals.prompt: A product bottle looks perfect but the generated label text mutates and the hand holding it gains an extra finger. Can I just add subtitles and publish?
evals.expected_output: Treat hand/anatomy and product geometry/text as identity/physics issues, not subtitle fixes; use label-safe blank plate plus post overlay, locally edit or regenerate the defective unit, and approve only after frame-step evidence.

evals.prompt: Use my two cat photos for a cute 60-second realistic short, but do not make it look like children's animation or plastic CGI.
evals.expected_output: Apply the pet overlay within the general workflow, keep real fur/material/environment, place cuteness in species behavior and timing, use anatomy/contact gates, and retain provider/model/user choice.
